_note: One unit = one lesson path in five steps. Write 'God' (the Muslim view shows 'Allah'). Verses by ref only (shown from src/data/ayahs.json); hadith by id only (shown from src/data/hadith.json). 'about' lines are our own words, never a translation.

intro.muslim: Yusuf's brothers threw him into a well when he was a boy. Years later, they stood before him in Egypt, hungry, not knowing who he was, and now he had all the power. Watch what he did with it.
intro.curious: Yusuf, known in the Bible as Joseph, was thrown into a well by his own brothers. Years later they stood before him in Egypt, hungry, not knowing who he was, and now he had all the power. Watch what he did.

muslim.situation: Someone who spread a hurtful rumour about you last year now needs your help with something only you can do.

options.label: Refuse, and tell everyone why.
options.feedback: They hurt you, and that's real. But Yusuf had far more reason, and far more power. See what he chose.

options.label: Help them, and let the past go.
options.feedback: That's what Yusuf did: "No blame on you today." Good character is most visible when you could do otherwise.

options.label: Help them, but remind them of what they did at every chance.
options.feedback: Helping is good; rubbing it in undoes much of it. See how Yusuf spoke.

options.label: Help them, and quietly keep your distance afterwards.
options.feedback: Forgiving doesn't mean trusting blindly. Yusuf's way is still the higher one: no blame.

curious.situation: Someone who spread a hurtful rumour about you last year now needs your help with something only you can do.

options.label: Refuse, and tell everyone why.
options.feedback: The hurt is real. But Yusuf had far more reason, and more power. See what he chose.

options.label: Help them, and let the past go.
options.feedback: That's what Yusuf did: "No blame on you today."

options.label: Help them, but remind them of what they did.
options.feedback: Helping is good; rubbing it in undoes much of it. See how Yusuf spoke.

options.label: Help them, and keep a careful distance afterwards.
options.feedback: Forgiving doesn't mean trusting blindly. Still, Yusuf's way goes further.

heading.muslim: What God teaches about good character
heading.curious: What Islam teaches about good character

quran.about: Yusuf tells his brothers there is no blame on them today, and prays that God forgive them.
God describes the Prophet ﷺ as being of a great moral character.
The righteous restrain their anger and pardon people; God loves those who do good.
Good and evil are not equal: repel evil with what is better, and an enemy may become a close friend.
Do not mock, insult or call one another names; avoid suspicion, spying and backbiting.

hadith.about: The best people are those best in character.
Real strength is controlling yourself when angry.

insights.text: Yusuf forgave at the moment he could have taken revenge (12:92). Good character shows most when you have the power to act otherwise.
The Prophet ﷺ tied good character to faith itself: the best of you are the best in character (Bukhari 6035), and righteousness is good character (Muslim 2553).

check.q: What did Yusuf say to his brothers when he revealed who he was?
check.why: No blame will there be upon you today; may God forgive you (12:92).

check.q: Why was Binyamin held back in Egypt?
options: The king's cup was found in his pack
He was arrested for stealing grain
check.why: The king's cup was found in Binyamin's pack, and by the law of the land he stayed.

check.q: How does 41:34 say to respond to evil?
check.why: Repel evil with what is better, and an enemy may become a close friend.

check.q: Who is strong, according to the hadith?
options: The one who wins every fight
The one who controls himself when angry
The one with the most friends
check.why: The strong one is the one who controls himself when angry.

check.q: Who are the best people, according to Bukhari 6035?
check.why: The best of you are those who are best in character.

reflection.muslim: Is there someone you're still holding something against? What would "no blame on you today" look like with them?
reflection.curious: Is there someone you could forgive, even partly? What would it cost you, and what might it free?
